title: Value of the client_secret query parameter of a Meta app access token call
summary: A synthetic value of client_secret beside client_id and grant_type=client_credentials in the query of an oauth/access_token request, in a raw request line, a curl URL and a query string that continues with another parameter.
rationale: Meta documents the client_secret query parameter of the oauth/access_token call, with client_id and grant_type client_credentials, as a carrier of the App Secret in server-side calls (contract claim carriers-client-secret-and-composite), and says to never share it. Meta states no length, alphabet or encoding (alphabet-not-settled), so the value is flagged because of the parameter it sits in, not because of its shape; the 32-character figure is the artifacts' scope only. The extent is the value only: the parameter name, the equals sign and the ampersand are outside it, and the app ID beside it is outside the span (the page does not call it non-secret, so it is not asserted as public). The pipe-joined access_token form is covered by meta-app-secret-in-app-id-pipe-access-token; this Case adds the client_secret parameter.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, redact-secret#1228 Group C). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: a value in the client_secret query parameter of an app access token call is treated as a credential whatever its shape. Meta documents the client_secret parameter of the app access token call (carrier existence only); the value admission, extent and a generic attribution are the project's decisions. No subtype is inferred, and no prefix, width or alphabet is claimed.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
